method_card.title: Shopping and Transactions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers shopping vocabulary, prices, sizes, polite request structures, and the demonstrative dieser/diese/dieses — all essential for the shop role-play.

GermanEnglish
einkaufen gehento go shopping (separable)
kaufento buy
bezahlento pay
der Preis (-e)price
teuerexpensive
billigcheap
im Angeboton offer / on sale
die Größe (-n)size
Ich möchte...I would like...
Ich hätte gern...I would like... (more formal)
Was kostet das?How much does that cost?
die Kasse (-n)till / checkout
dieser / diese / diesesthis (masc. / fem. / neut.)
(Higher) im Sonderangeboton special offer

Grammar focus 1 — Polite request structures (Sie register): In a shop, always use the formal Sie register. Key structures: Ich möchte + noun/infinitive (I would like), Ich hätte gern + noun (I would like — slightly more formal), Könnte ich bitte...? (Could I please...?). The infinitive goes to the end: Ich möchte diesen Pullover anprobieren.

Grammar focus 2 — demonstratives dieser/diese/dieses (this): These inflect for gender and case like definite articles, but start with dies-. Nominative: dieser (m), diese (f), dieses (n). Accusative: diesen (m), diese (f), dieses (n). So: Ich möchte diesen Pullover (accusative masculine — the Pullover is the direct object of möchte).

Grammar focus 3 — separable verb einkaufen gehen: In main clauses, the verb splits: Ich gehe samstags einkaufen. (I go shopping on Saturdays.) The prefix ein- moves to the clause end. In subordinate clauses it stays together: weil ich gern einkaufe.

Model: Guten Tag! Ich hätte gern diesen roten Pullover in Größe Medium. Was kostet er? — Er kostet zwanzig Euro. — Das ist ein bisschen teuer. Haben Sie etwas Billigeres? (Good day! I would like this red jumper in size medium. How much does it cost? — It costs twenty euros. — That is a bit expensive. Do you have something cheaper?)
steps: Learn shopping vocabulary including each noun's gender (der/die/das)
Master polite request structures: Ich möchte and Ich hätte gern in Sie register
Practise demonstrative dieser/diese/dieses — remember diesen for masculine accusative
Use the separable verb einkaufen gehen with the prefix at the end of the clause
Build full shop transactions combining price, size, and polite requests with capital nouns

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — shopping appears in speaking role-play, reading, writing and listening

worked_examples.question: What does 'Ich hätte gern diesen Pullover in Größe Medium' mean?

steps.label: Break down the key parts
steps.content: Ich hätte gern = I would like (polite formal). diesen Pullover = this jumper (accusative masculine — the Pullover is what I want).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I would like this jumper in size medium.

worked_examples.question: Why is it 'diesen Pullover' but 'diese Jacke'?

steps.label: Identify the case
steps.content: After Ich möchte / Ich hätte gern, the item is the direct object → accusative case.

steps.label: Apply the rule
steps.content: der Pullover is masculine. Demonstrative accusative masculine: dieser → diesen. die Jacke is feminine. Feminine accusative stays diese (no change from nominative).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Masculine accusative adds -en: diesen Pullover. Feminine accusative stays -e: diese Jacke.

bronze.question: Match the German shopping words to the English meaning
Match the German to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct demonstrative form

gaps.correct_explain: diesen is correct. der Pullover is masculine. After ich möchte, the noun is the direct object (accusative). Accusative masculine: dieser → diesen.

wrong.dieser: dieser is the masculine nominative form. After ich möchte (direct object), use the accusative: diesen.
wrong.dieses: dieses is the neuter form. der Pullover is masculine: diesen.

gaps.correct_explain: diese is correct. die Jacke is feminine. Feminine accusative demonstrative is diese (same as nominative).

wrong.diesen: diesen is masculine accusative. die Jacke is feminine — use diese.

gaps.correct_explain: hätte is the Konjunktiv II of haben — used for polite requests: Ich hätte gern = I would like. möchte is equally correct here.

wrong.habe: ich habe gern is not a standard polite request. Use hätte (Konjunktiv II) for 'I would like'.

gaps.correct_explain: Was kostet er? = How much does it cost? Was is standard in German for price questions.

wrong.Wie: Wie alone is incomplete. For prices, say Was kostet...? or Wie viel kostet...?

bronze.question: What does 'Haben Sie diesen Pullover in Größe Large?' mean?
options: Do you have this jumper in size large?
I would like this jumper in size large
This jumper is available in size large

bronze.question: What does 'Das ist im Angebot — es kostet nur fünf Euro' mean?
options: That is on offer — it only costs five euros
That is expensive — it costs five euros
That offer costs five euros more
That is not on offer yet

model_answers: I would like these shoes in size thirty-eight. How much do they cost?
hints: Was kosten sie = how much do they cost

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: I **go** shopping every Saturday and I **pay** at the checkout.

gaps.rule: Separable verb einkaufen gehen — prefix at end in main clause
gaps.correct_explain: gehe is the ich-form of gehen. In the separable verb einkaufen gehen, gehe sits at position 2 and the prefix ein- moves to the end: Ich gehe einkaufen.

wrong.kaufe: kaufe means 'I buy'. For 'I go shopping', use the separable verb: Ich gehe einkaufen.
wrong.einkaufe: In a main clause, separable verbs split — the conjugated verb sits at position 2: gehe. The prefix ein- goes to the end.

gaps.correct_explain: bezahle is the ich-form of bezahlen (to pay). Inseparable prefix be- means it stays together.

wrong.zahle: zahle means 'I count' (from zählen) or can be used in some contexts, but the standard verb for 'to pay' is bezahlen → bezahle.
wrong.bezahlt: bezahlt is the er/sie/es form. The subject is ich: use bezahle.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ich möchte dieses Pullover in Größe Medium.
silver.explanation: der Pullover is masculine. After ich möchte, the noun is the direct object (accusative). Accusative masculine demonstrative: dieser → diesen. dieses is the neuter form.
silver.translation: I would like this jumper in size medium.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: A return ticket to Berlin, please.

distractor_labels.Einen: wrong gender — die Fahrkarte is feminine, so use eine not einen (masculine accusative).

silver.source_text: How much do these trainers cost? Do you have them in size forty?
model_answers: Was kosten diese Turnschuhe? Haben Sie sie in Größe vierzig?

gold.source_text: I would like to buy this jacket, but it is too expensive. Do you have something cheaper? I only have twenty euros.
model_answers: Ich möchte diese Jacke kaufen, aber sie ist zu teuer. Haben Sie etwas Billiges? Ich habe nur zwanzig Euro.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a Gold-tier translation. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Check: Ich möchte + infinitive at end (kaufen), diese Jacke (feminine accusative demonstrative — stays diese), aber (coordinating conjunction — verb stays at position 2: sie ist), etwas Billiges (nominalised adjective — capital B, adjective ending -es after etwas/nichts). Accept Billiges or Günstigeres or similar. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: Excuse me, where is the till? I would like to pay.

distractor_labels.der: wrong gender — die Kasse is feminine, so use die not der.
distractor_labels.bezahlt: wrong form — after möchte (modal), use the infinitive: bezahlen, not bezahlt.
distractor_labels.möchten: wrong person — the subject is ich (I), so use möchte not möchten (wir/Sie form).

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are in a clothes shop in Germany. The shop assistant approaches you.

bullets.prompt: Greet the shop assistant and say you are looking for a jacket.
bullets.model_answer: Guten Tag! Ich suche eine Jacke. Können Sie mir helfen?
bullets.note: polite greeting + direct object accusative (eine Jacke — feminine), Sie register: Können Sie...?

bullets.prompt: Say you would like this blue jacket in size medium and ask how much it costs.
bullets.model_answer: Ich hätte gern diese blaue Jacke in Größe Medium. Was kostet sie?
bullets.note: Ich hätte gern (polite Sie-register), diese blaue Jacke (feminine accusative demonstrative + adjective ending after definite-like demonstrative: -e), Was kostet sie?

bullets.prompt: Say it is a bit expensive and ask if it is on offer.
bullets.model_answer: Das ist ein bisschen teuer. Ist sie im Angebot?
bullets.note: opinion + im Angebot (dative: in + dem = im)

bullets.prompt: Say you will take it and ask where the till is.
bullets.model_answer: Ich nehme sie. Wo ist die Kasse, bitte?
bullets.note: nehmen (to take) + pronoun sie referring to die Jacke (feminine), Wo ist...? question

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Ich möchte diesen roten Pullover kaufen, aber er ist leider zu teuer.
gold.correct_text: Ich möchte diesen roten Pullover kaufen, aber er ist leider zu teuer.
gold.translation: I would like to buy this red jumper, but unfortunately it is too expensive.

gold.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
gold.english: This offer is **only valid** until Saturday, so I **should** buy the jacket today.

gaps.rule: Verb conjugation — gelten (to be valid/to apply)
gaps.correct_explain: gilt is the er/sie/es form of gelten (to be valid). Note the stem-vowel change: gelten → er gilt.

wrong.gültig: gültig is an adjective (valid). As a predicate you can say ist gültig, but gilt is the more idiomatic choice.

gaps.correct_explain: sollte = should (Konjunktiv II of sollen). Here it expresses a personal recommendation. Ich sollte die Jacke kaufen — modal sollte at position 2, infinitive kaufen at the end.

wrong.soll: soll means 'am supposed to' (external instruction). sollte (Konjunktiv II) expresses personal advice — 'I should buy'.
wrong.muss: muss means 'must' (strong obligation). The sentence expresses mild advice, so sollte is more appropriate.
